name: Translations
description: Plays the game in another language. Choose a language for each game in Tools > Translations... (or make your own there: the patcher writes a file with every English line of the game, its menus, events, tips, tech names and the patcher's own windows, and a built-in editor shows each line in the game's font). The game uses the chosen language from its next start, with no re-patching; lines a translation leaves out, or gets wrong, stay English. Gender and plural words follow the villager or the number (for example il / elle, 1 pomme / 2 pommes). **On by default, and English until you choose a language: with English chosen the game is exactly as without this patch.** **Accented letters need "Render Unicode with In-Game Fonts" (the game's own font lacks most of them); letters outside Windows-1252 (for example Turkish ğ ş ı, Greek, Cyrillic, Chinese, Japanese or Cuneiform) show as "?" until a later version of that patch draws them.** **Words painted into pictures (buttons, the title screen, help pages) stay English.** **Text the game draws for the patcher (Cause of Death words, island event popups) stays English for now; the patcher's own windows are translated.** **Works the same with every other patch and in every population mode.** **Not yet seen in a running game.** The companion is "VVFP Translations.dll", started by VVFP Startup.dll; if it cannot be loaded, or the game's text is not the version a translation was made from, those lines stay English.
behavior_changes: At game start the companion reads "Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher Files\Translation\Translation.txt" (written by the patcher's Translations window; docs/translation-file-format.md). With no such file it returns at once and writes nothing.

Each translated line replaces the English where the game looks it up: the string table at 0x487208 (629 rows): each translated row's English pointer (+4); the visible literals outside the table by the address their loading instruction pushes (data/translations/vv1_strings.json).  A line is used only when the English it was made from is the English this game shows (the key's SHA-256), its placeholders match and its selects are well formed.

The patcher's own windows (Origins, Story / Cheat Upgrades, Custom Island Event) are translated as they open (a WH_CALLWNDPROCRET hook on the game's own thread, only when the file translates any of them).

Without "Render Unicode with In-Game Fonts" or "Use Unicode Font (overrides in-game fonts)" (their companion's VvfpGlyphsUtf8; Use Unicode Font's, which starts later, is loaded and started on first use), translations are given to the game in Windows-1252, '?' for what it cannot write.
explicit_non_changes: This row changes no executable bytes: the companion checks each site's stock bytes and writes them at run time through the shared all-or-none writer, and writes only the ones the chosen file needs; if any check fails it writes nothing, not even a table pointer, and the game stays English.
No save, record or game file is written; the game's own English text stays in memory unchanged.
With English chosen (no Translation.txt), nothing at all is written.
